churn_resistance.rationale: An Angular 23 upgrade would touch almost nothing but app.config.ts; data access, derivation and config are each behind a single module and typed. Deducted for four copies of the title/not-found logic and the never-evicting module-level cache, which are the things that will rot first.

findings.issue: withFetch() is deprecated in Angular v22 — FetchBackend is now the default HttpBackend (angular.dev/api/common/http/withFetch).
findings.suggestion: Replace provideHttpClient(withFetch()) with provideHttpClient(); the migration for this already ships with ng update to v22.

findings.issue: withEventReplay() is redundant in v22: provideClientHydration() now enables incremental hydration, which enables event replay itself (the CLI removed withEventReplay from its schematic, angular-cli#32996).
findings.suggestion: Use provideClientHydration() with no features, or withNoHttpTransferCache/etc. only if needed; drop withEventReplay().

findings.issue: Data loading is imperative Promise-based resolvers; Angular 22 graduated resource()/httpResource() to stable, which would add reactive reload, abort-on-param-change and status signals for free.
findings.suggestion: Keep the resolvers (still documented for SSR-complete HTML) or migrate the page data to httpResource/resource when client-side param changes (e.g. ?game=) need reactive refetching.

findings.issue: The dynamic document-title effect is duplicated verbatim in four page components (pokemon.page.ts:33, move.page.ts:86, ability.page.ts:47, type.page.ts:110).
findings.suggestion: Centralize with a custom TitleStrategy or a small directive/service so the "<h1> – Pokédex" rule and the not-found fallback live in one place.

findings.issue: The module-level responseCache never evicts entries for the life of the SSR process: memory grows with the API surface and stale data persists indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Add a simple TTL or size cap (or rely on HTTP caching headers) so a long-running process refreshes against the live API the spec treats as mutable.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared dependency but is never imported; the app binds native controls directly.
findings.suggestion: Remove @angular/forms, or if forms are added later use Signal Forms (stable in v22) rather than template-driven/reactive forms.

findings.issue: Leftover CLI scaffold comments ("Example Express Rest API endpoints can be defined here") and default port 4000 boilerplate make the server entry read as unreviewed template output.
findings.suggestion: Trim the template comments to the ones that reflect this app's actual decisions (the allowedHosts note is worth keeping).

findings.issue: Hand-rolled setTimeout debounce with an ad-hoc timer field; util.ts:17 also parses resource URLs by regex where the URL API would be more robust.
findings.suggestion: Extract a tiny debounce helper and use new URL(url).pathname for id extraction so both edge cases (query strings, no trailing slash) are handled by the platform.

summary: A genuinely current Angular 22 codebase: signal inputs, control-flow templates, TransferState-configured data access behind a single service, modern SSR/hydration, and a real HTTP 404 via RESPONSE_INIT, with lean dependencies and almost no upgrade surface. The only legacy residue is v21-era provider wiring (deprecated withFetch, redundant withEventReplay) and a data layer on resolvers rather than the now-stable resource()/httpResource(). Maintainability deductions come from four copies of the title/not-found logic and a never-evicting module-level cache.

apis.replacement: provideHttpClient() — FetchBackend is the default HttpBackend since v22 (angular.dev/api/common/http/withFetch)
provideClientHydration() — incremental hydration (includes event replay) is the v22 default (angular-cli#32996)
resource()/httpResource() (stable in v22) is the newer data-loading primitive, though resolvers remain documented for SSR
